component.name: OxiGuitar
component.summary: View, edit and play guitar tablature and scores

description.p: OxiGuitar opens Guitar Pro files (.gp, .gpx, .gp5, .gp4 and .gp3) and shows them as standard notation and tablature, in four layouts, with any set of tracks together. It edits and saves them, exports them to PDF, and plays them, with a cursor on the beat being heard.

ul.li: Playback from the caret or a selection, with loop, count-in, metronome, speed from 25 to 200 % and a mixer for every track
Your system's General MIDI sound set out of the box, and better sounds you add: SoundFont (SF2, SF3, DLS) and SFZ instruments with recorded guitars, basses and drums
Note entry and editing with Guitar Pro 8's keys: effects, chords, lyrics, tracks, tunings and transposition
Every file format, sound and audio output is a plugin, and anyone can write one

description.p: No telemetry: OxiGuitar never uploads anything and downloads nothing.

screenshot.caption: Playing an eight-track song, with the cursor on the beat being heard and each track's mixer
Editing a bend on the tablature, with the palette of tools and the Inspector
The light interface, with lyrics under a melody

description.p: The MIDI plugin's settings drop-down lists reach the window's edge and follow it when it is resized, so long option strings are never cut off.

A plugin's settings window opens twice as large (960 by 640), and its drop-down lists stretch to the window's edge and follow it when it is resized, in the settings window and in the panels that show a plugin's tab. The names of sounds are long and were cut short by drop-downs as wide as their ...

Publishing a release tells the package repositories and the Homebrew tap by itself (publish.yml, #226, as each plugin's does), so the apt and dnf repositories and the tap follow without running their workflows by hand.
The apt and dnf packages also recommend the ALSA and PipeWire audio output plugins, so OxiGuitar has a way to play sound once installed.
The plugins move to repositories and packages of their own: OxiGuitar itself no longer carries them, and the apt and dnf packages recommend the Guitar Pro and MIDI plugins.
Amp models (NAM) and WAV export, the sound plugin renamed MIDI, dialogs that say what is missing, and the plugin interface frozen at 1.4 before the plugins move to repositories of their own.
Recorded guitars, basses and drums: SFZ instruments play in the sound plugin, picked per role in its settings.
The player: transport, cursor, loop, count-in, metronome, speed and mixer, with SoundFont sound sets.
The editor: note entry, effects, chords, lyrics, tracks, transposition, and saving Guitar Pro files.
Plugins: every file format is a plugin, with a plugin manager and a developer guide.
The viewer: Guitar Pro files as notation and tablature, four layouts, PDF export.
